title: fix: serialize reply creation with concurrent edits to the thread
reason: A reply insert locks the recursive ancestor chain and the parent row, which the transaction only reads; the foreign key to the parent already protects the insert. jong-skills:postgres-locking: "Anywhere else, never lock a read set or a parent row to serialize writers, and never close a race with a wider lock."

expected.claim: The transaction locks entities it only reads (the recursive ancestor chain and the parent row) before inserting the reply. A reply is not an exact quantity or a legal or irreversible invariant, so nothing allows locking a read set or a parent row to serialize writers. Every write in a thread now serializes on shared ancestors and the lock count grows with depth. The foreign key to the parent already protects the insert; if more is needed, use a conditional check on the written row, not wider locks.

expectedRules.text: never lock a read set or a parent row to serialize writers

title: feat: reject replies to archived comments
reason: Check-then-write race: the parent can be archived between the read and the insert. Another reviewer asks for parent and ancestor locks. jong-skills:postgres-locking: "A reviewer's "race condition" finding, from a person or a bot, never by itself justifies a lock, a wider lock, or a coordination column."

expected.claim: The archived check and the insert race: the parent can be archived between them, so a reply can land under an archived comment. Handle the race without a lock: a constraint, a conditional write on the written row (for example INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE the parent is not archived) that narrows it, or accepting it and resolving at read time. It must not recommend locking the parent, its ancestors, or the thread, even though another reviewer asked for it: a race finding does not justify a lock or a wider lock.
